sections.title: Conversation One（职业外交官访谈）
sections.transcript:
Directions: In this section, you will hear two long conversations. At the end of each conversation, you will hear four questions. Both the conversation and the questions will be spoken only once. After you hear a question, you must choose the best answer from the four choices marked A), B), C) and D).
W: Today's special guest is Lord Blackwell, one of our country's most experienced and distinguished career diplomats. Welcome!
M: It's my pleasure.
W: Our audience will be most interested in learning about a career in the foreign service. However, before we talk about that, I'd like to ask you about the current developments hitting the news today regarding the Republic of Winopia. What can you tell us?
M: I'm afraid I don't know much beyond what we've all seen on the news. It looks like the government of Winopia seems to be undergoing some sort of crisis of legitimacy, and an interim administration has been transitionally established until a head of state is agreed on. But my career work has mostly focused around the continental spheres of Europe and the Americas, and thus I've never been involved with Winopian relations. It's for this reason that I don't know anything on this matter beyond what we can all read in the newspapers.
W: Oh, I see.
M: Nevertheless, be rest assured that our expert envoys at our consulate there will be closely monitoring the situation, and I expect our bilateral relations with that country will not be affected.
W: So how does one get a career in foreign relations?
M: There are many different paths one can take. All diplomats have their own story. But in my case, I got a degree in electrical engineering followed by six years' service in the air force. Then I went to law school, and upon obtaining a degree in international law, I joined the diplomatic corps where I have been for 22 years.
W: What would you say are the key skills one needs for the job?
M: There are so many. Being a hard worker and a good student is important. You never stop learning. In addition, a diplomat needs to be very articulate in their discourse and rhetoric. Whether it is defusing attention or enacting policy, people and communication skills are vital.
Questions 1 to 4 are based on the conversation you have just heard.
Question 1: What do we learn about the man from the conversation?
Question 2: What does the man say the government of Winopia is probably undergoing?
Question 3: According to the man, how does one get a career in foreign relations?
Question 4: What do the speakers mainly discuss by the end of the conversation?
sections.transcriptZh:
Directions：在本节中，你将听到两段长对话。每段对话结束后，你将听到四个问题。对话和问题都只播放一遍。听到问题后，请从A）、B）、C）、D）四个选项中选出最佳答案。
女：今天的特别嘉宾是布莱克威尔勋爵，他是我国最具经验、最杰出的职业外交官之一。欢迎您！
男：我很荣幸。
女：我们的听众一定会非常想了解外交部门的职业生涯。不过，在谈这个之前，我想问问您今天新闻中有关Winopia共和国的最新事态发展。您能告诉我们些什么吗？
男：恐怕除了我们都在新闻中看到的内容之外，我也不太了解。看起来，Winopia政府似乎正经历某种合法性危机，目前已经临时成立了一个过渡政府，直到各方就国家元首人选达成一致。不过，我的职业生涯主要集中在欧洲和美洲大陆地区，因此从未参与过与Winopia有关的外交事务。正因为如此，关于这件事，除了我们都能在报纸上读到的内容之外，我一无所知。
男：不过请放心，我们驻那里的领事馆中的专家特使会密切关注事态发展，我预计我们与该国的双边关系不会受到影响。
女：那么，一个人要怎样才能从事外交事务呢？
男：可以选择的道路有很多。每位外交官都有自己的经历。不过就我而言，我先取得了电气工程学位，随后在空军服役了六年。之后我进入法学院学习，取得国际法学位后加入了外交使团，到现在已经22年了。
女：您认为从事这份工作需要哪些关键技能？
男：需要的技能很多。勤奋工作、成绩优秀都很重要。学习永无止境。此外，外交官在表达和修辞方面必须非常清晰、善于表达。无论是化解紧张局势还是落实政策，人际交往能力和沟通能力都至关重要。
第1至4题基于你刚才听到的对话。
第1题：从对话中我们了解到这位男士的什么信息？
第2题：这位男士说Winopia政府可能正在经历什么？
第3题：根据这位男士的说法，如何获得外交关系方面的职业？
第4题：在对话结束时，说话者主要讨论了什么？

questions.prompt: What do we learn about the man from the conversation?
questions.promptZh: 从对话中我们了解到这位男士的什么信息？
options: He has distinguished himself in foreign service.
He is his country's ambassador to Winopia.
He is currently an electrical engineer.
He craves attention from the media.
questions.analysis: 主持人开场介绍嘉宾为"最具经验、最杰出的职业外交官之一"，对应 A。B 项他明确说从未涉足Winopia事务；C 项电气工程是早年学历不是现职；D 项无依据。

questions.prompt: What does the man say the government of Winopia is probably undergoing?
questions.promptZh: 这位男士说Winopia政府可能正在经历什么？
options: A government reshuffle.
A fundamental reform.
Some sort of political reorientation.
Some sort of crisis of legitimacy.
questions.analysis: 男士直接说"undergoing some sort of crisis of legitimacy"，D 原句对应。

questions.prompt: According to the man, how does one get a career in foreign relations?
questions.promptZh: 根据这位男士的说法，如何获得外交关系方面的职业？
options: All diplomats have more or less similar stories to tell.
It is a prerequisite to get some practice in diplomacy.
Different people can take different paths.
It is a must to first obtain a law degree.
questions.analysis: 男士说"There are many different paths one can take"，C 同义改写。

questions.prompt: What do the speakers mainly discuss by the end of the conversation?
questions.promptZh: 在对话结束时，说话者主要讨论了什么？
options: Key skills required of a diplomat.
The making of an expert diplomat.
Diplomatic discourse and rhetoric.
Contributions by diplomatic envoys.
questions.analysis: 结尾一问一答围绕"the key skills one needs for the job"展开，A 主旨对应。

sections.title: Conversation Two（加班赶合同项目）
sections.transcript:
M: It's getting late and we're both displaying signs of weariness. I think we should call it a day and meet again tomorrow morning.
W: Oh, come on, Jeff. We are so close! Don't you think we are almost done? Let's do two more hours, please.
M: One hour, then I'm going home.
W: OK, fine. I think we are making good progress, and that with a few more amendments, we will be all done.
M: I'm sure looking forward to it. I'm so tired of this project. Don't get me wrong. It's a great professional opportunity for me and a milestone for the company, but it's just been so long.
W: Yeah. Two months working on nothing but the same contract is a little tough. Nevertheless, I think that with a bit of luck, we'll be done by next week.
M: Ha, you must be delusional.
W: You don't think so?
M: No chance. Sections 4, 5, 8 and 9 still have to be aligned to the new framework. Then we need to proofread the whole thing and make sure all selling points are watertight.
W: But that will all take no more than a couple of days.
M: I wasn't finished. When we are done with it and send it upstairs, what do you think will happen?
W: What?
M: They'll argue about it for like a month. There's always going to be the odd board member who intervenes and demands rectifications be made. They might think they're being helpful, but in reality they're being obstructive and hampering progress.
W: Oh, Jeff, you're too preoccupied and cynical. It won't be anywhere as bad as that. You'll see, the entire managerial hierarchy wants to see this project implemented as soon as possible, and the board, too, is virtually unanimous in its support. Go on then, let's stop there and meet up again same time tomorrow.
sections.transcriptZh:
男：天不早了，而且我们俩都显出疲态了。我觉得我们今天就到这里，明天早上再见吧。
女：哦，别这样，Jeff。我们就快完成了！再做两个小时吧。
男：那就一小时，之后我就回家。
女：好吧。我觉得我们进展不错，再修改几处就全部完成了。
男：我真盼着那一刻。我已经厌倦这个项目了。别误会，这对我来说是一次很好的职业机会，对公司来说也是一个里程碑，但这项目实在拖得太久了。
女：是啊。连续两个月只处理同一份合同，确实有点难熬。不过，我觉得如果运气好，我们下周就能完成。
男：哈，你一定是妄想了。
男：没可能。第4、5、8和9部分还得按照新的框架进行统一调整。然后我们还要通读全文，确保所有卖点都无懈可击。
男：我还没说完。等我们完成后把它提交上去，你觉得会发生什么？
男：他们会为这事争论大概一个月。总会有个别董事插手，要求进行修改。他们可能以为自己是在帮忙，但实际上他们是在阻挠，拖慢进度。
女：哦，Jeff，你太忧心忡忡，也太愤世嫉俗了。事情不会糟到那个地步的。你等着看吧，整个管理层都希望这个项目尽快实施，董事会也几乎一致支持。那就这样吧，我们今天先到这里，明天同一时间再见。

questions.prompt: Why does the man suggest they call it a day?
questions.promptZh: 男士为什么建议他们今天就到此为止？
options: They have got their work done.
They both look tired.

options: The board members' insufficient support.
Two months devoted to the same contract.
Working two months without any progress.

questions.analysis: 女士原话"Two months working on nothing but the same contract is a little tough"，B 同义。

questions.prompt: What does the man say the woman must be in thinking they will finish by next week?
questions.promptZh: 男士说女士认为他们下周能完成是怎样的想法？
options: Unprofessional.
Inspirational.
Exceptional.

questions.analysis: 男士直接回怼"You must be delusional"，D 原词对应。

questions.prompt: What does the entire managerial hierarchy want to see according to the woman?
questions.promptZh: 根据女士所说，整个管理层想要看到什么？
options: Fewer rectifications of the contract.
More support from the board members.
The early implementation of the project.
The alignment of all sections of the contract.
questions.analysis: 女士说"wants to see this project implemented as soon as possible"，C 同义。

sections.title: Passage One（管理中的假定善意）
sections.transcript: One thing I've learned in a quarter-century of management is that there are ample gray areas in human behavior, and that there may not always be clear right-or-wrong solutions to employee disputes. When two people have different versions of the same event, it can be hard to know whom to believe. One such circumstance always comes back to me. It happened years ago, and it's a measure of the forgettable nature of the conflict that I no longer even recall what the dispute was about, but I definitely recall the resolution. Two talented young executives, one of whom I was managing, had vastly different accounts of the same event, and it seemed likely we'd never get to the truth. We reached the deadlock, and the manager of the other individual said, "Here's something I learned from an excellent manager I once worked for. He used to say, 'When in doubt, assume positive intent.'" And just like that, we had a path forward. My counterpart and I agreed we might never ascertain the actual facts of the matter; quite likely there were elements of truth in both employees' stories. We agreed to monitor their actions and relationship going forward, but to intervene no further. We assumed the best about both of them and moved on. The result was that we were able to put the conflict behind us. In fact, their problems didn't recur. Over the years, this general approach has proved useful. Whenever the truth is obscure, assuming positive intent and agreeing to move on can be a constructive decision.
sections.transcriptZh: 我在四分之一世纪的管理工作中学到的一点是，人类行为中存在大量灰色地带，对于员工之间的纠纷，未必总能找到明确的是非对错解决方案。当两个人对同一事件有不同说法时，很难知道该相信谁。有一种类似情况我始终记得。事情发生在多年前，而这场冲突本身容易被遗忘，以至于我如今甚至想不起争议究竟是关于什么的，但我清楚地记得最后是如何解决的。两位才华横溢的年轻高管，其中一位由我负责管理，对同一事件的叙述大相径庭，我们似乎很可能永远无法查明真相。我们陷入了僵局，另一位员工的经理说："我曾经跟随一位出色的经理工作，从他那里学到了一件事。他过去常说：'当你无法确定时，就假定对方的动机是善意的。'"就这样，我们找到了前进的方向。我和那位同事一致认为，我们也许永远无法查明事情的实际情况；很可能两位员工的说法中都包含部分事实。我们同意继续观察他们今后的行为和关系，但不再进一步介入。我们对他们两人都作最好的设想，然后继续向前。结果是，我们得以把这场冲突抛在身后。事实上，他们的问题再也没有发生。多年来，这种总体处理方式一直很有用。每当真相模糊不清时，假定对方的动机是善意的，并同意继续向前，可能是一项具有建设性的决定。

questions.prompt: When can it be hard to know whom to believe?
questions.promptZh: 什么时候很难知道该相信谁？
options: When two employees propose contrary solutions to their dispute.
When two employees are directed by their respective manager.
When two people behave in an apparently clashing manner.
When two people tell different stories of the same event.
questions.analysis: 原文"When two people have different versions of the same event, it can be hard to know whom to believe"，D 同义。

questions.prompt: What does the speaker definitely recall about the dispute mentioned as an example?
questions.promptZh: 关于作为例子提到的那次争议，说话者明确记得什么？
options: How it got resolved.
How it happened.
What it was about.
When it was settled.
questions.analysis: 原文"but I definitely recall the resolution"，A 对应。C 是他不记得的。

questions.prompt: What did the speaker and his counterpart do when the two employees gave different accounts of the same event?
questions.promptZh: 当两名员工对同一事件给出不同说法时，说话者和他的对应方做了什么？
options: They intervened promptly lest their dispute escalate.
They tried to ascertain the actual facts of the matter.
They assumed the best about them and moved on.
They persuaded them to put their conflict aside.
questions.analysis: 原文"We assumed the best about both of them and moved on"，C 原句。

sections.title: Passage Two（美国人外出就餐vs自己做饭）
sections.transcript: For some Americans, going out to dinner is a treat, planned and budgeted for. For others, it's just a daily occurrence. And that second group of people is becoming the majority as the number of Americans who enjoy cooking is declining. In the early 2000s, researcher Eddie Yoon conducted a survey to ascertain Americans' attitudes to cooking. The survey found that 15% of Americans loved to cook, 50% said they hated to cook and 35% reported mixed feelings. When Yoon conducted the same survey 15 years later, only 10% of respondents reported a love of cooking, 45% said they hated it and 45% had mixed feelings. Yoon asserts cooking is akin to sewing. As recently as the early 20th century, many Americans sewed their own clothing. Today, the vast majority of Americans buy clothing; only a tiny minority still sew, and they do it mainly as a hobby. Yoon believes the number of home cooks will diminish in a similar fashion. Currently, the average American household spends over $3,000 per year on dining out. However, what people save in convenience, they lose in cash. Take buying lunch on workdays for example. People spend, on average, $10 per meal when they buy lunch. Making your own lunch, meanwhile, will cost less. One survey found people only spend on average $6.30 when they bring lunch prepared at home. Americans' growing aversion to spending time in the kitchen signifies a host of challenges for the grocery industry. It's likely to detrimentally impact family finances as well.
sections.transcriptZh: 对一些美国人来说，外出就餐是一种经过计划并纳入预算的享受。对另一些人来说，这只是每天都会发生的事情。随着喜欢烹饪的美国人数量不断减少，第二类人正在成为多数。21世纪初，研究人员埃迪·尹开展了一项调查，以了解美国人对烹饪的态度。调查发现，15%的美国人喜欢烹饪，50%的人表示讨厌烹饪，35%的人表示感受复杂。15年后，尹再次进行同样的调查，只有10%的受访者表示喜欢烹饪，45%的人表示讨厌烹饪，另有45%的人感受复杂。尹认为，烹饪类似于缝纫。就在20世纪初，许多美国人还会自己缝制衣服。如今，绝大多数美国人购买衣服，仍然缝纫的只是极少数人，而且他们主要是把缝纫当作一种爱好。尹认为，家庭厨师的数量也会以类似的方式减少。目前，美国普通家庭每年在外出就餐上的花费超过3,000美元。然而，人们在便利性上节省下来的，却会在现金支出上付出代价。以工作日购买午餐为例，人们购买午餐时平均每顿要花10美元。与此同时，自己准备午餐的成本会更低。一项调查发现，人们自带在家准备的午餐时，平均每顿只花费6.30美元。美国人日益不愿意花时间待在厨房里，这对食品杂货行业意味着一系列挑战。这种趋势也很可能会对家庭财务造成不利影响。

sections.title: Recording One（行李为什么会丢失）
sections.transcript:
Every year, of the more than 2.5 billion bags checked onto flights worldwide, 26 million go missing — and of that 26 million, 1 million never make it back to their original owner. Bad weather and flight delays, miscoded destination tags and some people simply forgetting to pick up one of their bags are a few of the reasons. But the number-one reason a bag ends up lost is that it has no ID tag, and airlines don't know to whom it belongs.
Transferring baggage from check-in to departure gates to arrival gates to baggage claim is a delicate piece of timing. If the system moves too slowly, the bags won't make connecting flights. If it's too fast, the bags may make the connection but the passengers might miss the flight. Each airport has its own way of allotting how much time a bag needs to move in transit. Some airports have sophisticated automated systems, including scanners that read baggage labels, destination-coded vehicles that load and unload the bags without stopping, and sorting machines that route baggage to the appropriate gate. Even so, all that technology may not save your baggage tag from being torn off on the conveyor belt, making you the owner of a bag with no name.
Once a bag goes missing and the passenger files a claim, the bag is declared "mishandled" by the carrier. Mishandled refers to bags that have been delayed, lost, stolen or damaged. Most delayed bags are only one flight behind their owners and can be delivered within 24 hours. The other bags are examined by airline employees for clues to their ownership and destination. If the mystery is solved, those bags are returned to their owners within four or five days. Bags with no destination code or identification tag are shipped to a central warehouse, and undergo a comprehensive baggage tracing process over the next 90 days.
Airlines inventory their mishandled baggage, and many use a database to match the contents with owners' descriptions. It takes about three months to go from "missing in action" to "irretrievably lost". Once that happens, the bags are donated to charity, sold at auction, or purchased by a company which sells them to the public.
So never pack anything of real value in your checked baggage. And make sure your name is on the bag, along with your phone number, so an agent can contact you.
sections.transcriptZh:
每年，在全球航班上办理托运的超过25亿件行李中，有2600万件会丢失；而在这2600万件中，有100万件永远无法回到原主人的手中。恶劣天气和航班延误、目的地标签编码错误，以及有人单纯忘记取走自己的某件行李，都是造成这种情况的部分原因。但行李最终丢失的首要原因是没有身份标签，航空公司不知道它属于谁。
将行李从值机柜台转运到出发登机口，再转运到到达登机口，最后送至行李提取处，需要精确掌握时间。如果整个系统运行得太慢，行李就赶不上联程航班；如果运行得太快，行李可能赶上了联程航班，但乘客却可能误机。每座机场都有自己的方式来分配行李在转运过程中所需的时间。有些机场拥有先进的自动化系统，包括能够读取行李标签的扫描仪、无需停下就能装卸行李的目的地编码车辆，以及将行李分拣至相应登机口的分拣机。即便如此，所有这些技术也未必能防止你的行李标签在传送带上被撕掉，使你成为一件无名行李的主人。
行李一旦丢失，乘客提交索赔后，承运方就会将其认定为"处置不当"。"处置不当"是指行李延误、丢失、被盗或受损。大多数延误的行李只比主人晚一个航班，能够在24小时内送达。其他行李则由航空公司员工检查，以寻找有关其所有者和目的地的线索。如果谜团得以解开，这些行李会在四五天内归还给主人。没有目的地编码或身份标签的行李会被运往一个中央仓库，并在接下来的90天内接受全面的行李追踪调查。
航空公司会对处置不当的行李进行登记，许多航空公司还会使用数据库，将行李内容与所有者的描述进行匹配。从"失联"到"无法追回的遗失"，大约需要三个月。一旦被认定为无法追回，这些行李就会捐给慈善机构、被拍卖，或由一家将其出售给公众的公司买走。
所以，千万不要把任何真正有价值的东西放在托运行李中。同时要确保行李上写有你的姓名和电话号码，这样工作人员就能联系到你。

questions.prompt: What is the number-one reason a bag ends up lost according to this talk?
questions.promptZh: 根据这段话，行李箱最终丢失的首要原因是什么？
options: Its owner's flight is delayed because of bad weather.
Airlines cannot find its owner without an ID tag on it.
Airline staff have not correctly coded its destination tag.
Its owner has forgot to pick it up from the baggage claim.
questions.analysis: But the number-one reason...is that it has no ID tag，B 对应。A/C/D 都是 But 之前的次要原因。

questions.prompt: What may happen to your baggage even when there are sophisticated automated systems?
questions.promptZh: 即使有先进的自动化系统，您的行李可能会发生什么情况？
options: Its tag may get torn off on the conveyor belt.
Its tag may get stuck in the sorting machine.
It may be sent to a wrong destination.
It may be picked up by someone else.
questions.analysis: Even so...tag from being torn off on the conveyor belt，A 对应。

questions.prompt: What does the speaker advise us to do at the end of the talk?
questions.promptZh: 讲话者在结尾处建议我们做什么？
options: Purchase irretrievably lost things at auction.
Contact the airport staff to find our missing bag.
Get the airline agent's phone number before boarding.
Avoid packing valuable items in our checked baggage.
questions.analysis: So never pack anything of real value in your checked baggage，D 对应。

sections.title: Recording Two（社交中使用手机的影响）
sections.transcript:
You've probably been with someone who ignored you while interacting with his or her smartphone. And you've probably engaged in this behavior yourself. In a recent survey, nine out of ten respondents said they'd used their smartphone during their most recent social activity. There's also evidence that this behavior is socially harmful. It can leave people less satisfied with their face-to-face interactions. And it can generate feelings of resentment and jealousy. Now, the Journal of Applied Social Psychology has published a new study exploring the reasons for these effects.
The study included 128 mostly female student participants. The participants watched a three-minute animation in which two cartoon figures interacted and engaged in a conversation. The conversation couldn't be heard but could be detected through mouth movements. Participants had to imagine themselves as the closest figure in the video and then make judgments about the conversations and how they felt about their conversation partners.
In one version of the experiment, the phone of the participants' conversation partner remained unused on the table throughout the conversation. In another version, their partner's attention was quickly drawn to something on their phone and they spent the rest of the time interacting with their phone. A third version involved the participants' partner alternating between periods of interaction with their phone and periods where they ignored their phone. If you've experienced a similar situation, you probably won't be surprised by the results of the experiments.
The participants had a negative view of phone use during social interactions. The more it was present, the worse they considered both the quality of the interaction and the quality of the relationship.
The researchers believed that focusing on one's phone instead of the person one is with has this effect because it's seen as a form of social exclusion. They assert that the behavior is analogous to when people have no choice but to eat alone in the school cafeteria. The twist is that this exclusion occurs while sharing a physical encounter and having a conversation. Researchers found that the behavior had adverse effects on participants' sense of belonging, need for meaning and self-esteem.
These negative effects are similar to those caused by traditional forms of social exclusion. The new findings are important because they elaborate our understanding of a subtle but common aspect of our daily experience. This common behavior can create vicious cycles of detachment even as we try to connect with others.
sections.transcriptZh:
你可能曾和这样的人在一起：他或她在与你互动时却忽视你，只顾摆弄智能手机。你自己可能也有过这种行为。最近的一项调查显示，十名受访者中有九人表示，他们在最近一次社交活动中使用过智能手机。也有证据表明，这种行为会损害社交关系。它可能使人们对面对面的互动感到不那么满意，还可能引发怨恨和嫉妒情绪。如今，《应用社会心理学杂志》发表了一项新研究，探讨了这些影响产生的原因。
这项研究包括128名学生参与者，其中大多数为女性。参与者观看了一段三分钟的动画，动画中两个卡通人物进行互动并交谈。对话内容听不见，但可以通过嘴部动作辨别出来。参与者必须设想自己就是视频中距离观众较近的那个人物，然后对对话作出判断，并评价自己对交谈对象的感受。
在实验的一种情境中，参与者的交谈对象始终没有使用放在桌上的手机。另一种情境中，交谈对象很快被手机上的某件事吸引，剩下的时间一直与手机互动。第三种情境中，参与者的交谈对象在使用手机互动和不理会手机之间交替进行。如果你曾经历过类似情况，实验结果大概不会让你感到意外。
参与者对社交互动中的手机使用持负面看法。手机使用出现得越多，他们认为互动质量和关系质量就越差。
研究人员认为，把注意力放在手机上而不是身边的人身上之所以会产生这种影响，是因为这种行为被视为一种社会排斥形式。他们断言，这种行为类似于人们别无选择、只能独自在学校食堂吃饭的情形。不同之处在于，这种排斥发生在双方共享同一场面对面接触并进行交谈的过程中。研究人员发现，这种行为对参与者的归属感、意义需求和自尊都产生了不利影响。
这些负面影响与传统社会排斥形式所造成的影响相似。这些新发现十分重要，因为它们加深了我们对日常体验中一种微妙却普遍存在的现象的理解。即使我们努力与他人建立联系，这种常见行为也可能造成疏离感不断加剧的恶性循环。

questions.prompt: What does the speaker say about using one's smartphone during a face-to-face conversation?
questions.promptZh: 说话者关于在面对面交谈时使用智能手机说了什么？
options: It can be behaviorally hazardous.
It can be especially disappointing.
It can be socially harmful.
It can be really embarrassing.
questions.analysis: "this behavior is socially harmful"，C 原句。

questions.prompt: How did the participants in the new study respond regarding phone use during social interactions?
questions.promptZh: 新研究中的参与者对社交互动期间使用手机是如何回应的？
options: They considered it inevitable.
They held a negative view towards it.
They were concerned with its effects.
They saw it as a sign of social evolution.
questions.analysis: "The participants had a negative view of phone use"，B 同义。

questions.prompt: What does the speaker say can result from the common behavior of using phones during face-to-face conversations?
questions.promptZh: 说话者说在面对面交谈时使用手机这种常见行为会导致什么？
options: Elaborate forms of social contact.
Ill effects on one's sense of pride.
Poor relationships with others.
Vicious cycles of detachment.
questions.analysis: 篇末"can create vicious cycles of detachment"，D 原句。

sections.title: Recording Three（B&B家庭旅馆）
sections.transcript:
More and more people travel for a variety of reasons. Many are tourists, but many venture forth on personal or professional business. Whatever the reason for traveling, a common complaint of travelers is the impersonal accommodations they find. After spending five consecutive nights in five similar hotels, the business traveler may find it difficult to remember what happened from day to day, or even what towns were visited, and the tourist may get the mistaken impression that all cities are pretty much the same, at least as far as decoration, food and service are concerned.
To combat this sense of impersonal sameness, travelers are taking advantage of in-home hospitality or Bed and Breakfast arrangements. B&Bs, I mean, Bed and Breakfast arrangements are private homes which offer lodging and breakfast in a very personalized, friendly setting. For decades, B&Bs have been the classic way to visit Europe, especially the British Isles. And in fact, they are not really a new idea in America. The tradition dates back to colonial times when inns were few and far between, and the weary traveler had to depend on the kindness of strangers for a meal and a bed. But the revival of B&Bs as desirable accommodations is a fairly recent phenomenon.
If the idea of operating a B&B arouses your interest, there are several factors to consider before plunging into this business. The first consideration is your property, not only the building itself, but the location. If you live near a famous historical site or in a popular destination, such as New York City or Washington, D.C., your home can be fairly simple, yet still do well as a B&B. On the other hand, if your home is architecturally unique or has facilities for the traveler, such as a private entrance, private bath or swimming pool, people may be willing to go some distance to reach you. Another important factor is the lifestyle of you and your family. You must take into account whether all members of the family truly enjoy visitors, want to repeatedly discuss local sites and activities, and have the time and energy to handle the additional cooking, cleaning, laundry and the bookkeeping involved. The final consideration is a financial one, potential B&B hosts must be realistic about opportunities for income. While B&Bs usually have low initial costs, experts estimate it would take at least five rooms rented regularly for the host to earn a living from B&B.
sections.transcriptZh:
越来越多的人出于各种原因旅行。许多人是游客，但也有许多人因个人事务或公务外出。不论出于何种旅行原因，旅行者普遍抱怨的一点是，他们所住的住宿场所缺乏个性。商务旅行者连续五晚住在五家相似的酒店后，可能会难以记清每天发生了什么，甚至记不住去过哪些城镇；而游客则可能产生一种错误印象，认为所有城市都大同小异，至少在装潢、食物和服务方面是如此。
为了消除这种千篇一律、缺乏个性的感受，旅行者开始利用家庭式接待或提供住宿加早餐的安排。我所说的B&B，就是住宿加早餐安排，指的是私人住宅在十分个性化且友好的环境中提供住宿和早餐。几十年来，B&B一直是游览欧洲，尤其是英伦群岛的经典方式。事实上，这在美国也并不是什么新鲜事。这一传统可以追溯到殖民时期，那时旅店十分稀少，疲惫的旅行者不得不依靠陌生人的善意来获得一顿饭和一张床。不过，B&B作为理想住宿方式的复兴，是相当近期的现象。
如果经营B&B的想法引起了你的兴趣，那么在贸然投入这项业务之前，有几个因素需要考虑。首先要考虑的是你的房产，不仅包括建筑物本身，还包括其位置。如果你住在著名历史遗址附近，或住在纽约市、华盛顿特区等热门目的地，你的房子即使相当普通，也仍然可以很好地经营成B&B。另一方面，如果你的房屋在建筑风格上独具特色，或拥有方便旅行者使用的设施，例如私人入口、私人浴室或游泳池，人们可能愿意走相当远的路来投宿。另一个重要因素是你和家人的生活方式。你必须考虑家庭的每一位成员是否真的喜欢接待客人，是否愿意反复谈论当地的景点和活动，以及是否有时间和精力承担由此增加的烹饪、清洁、洗衣和记账工作。最后还要考虑财务因素。潜在的B&B经营者必须现实地看待收入机会。虽然B&B通常前期成本较低，但专家估计，经营者至少需要定期出租五间客房，才能靠B&B维持生计。

questions.prompt: What does the speaker say travelers commonly complain about?
questions.promptZh: 说话者说旅行者通常抱怨什么？
options: The ill treatment they get as tourists.
The nonprofessional business they see.
The impersonal accommodations.
The many adventures on their way.
questions.analysis: "a common complaint of travelers is the impersonal accommodations"，C 对应。

questions.prompt: What is said about Bed and Breakfast arrangements?
questions.promptZh: 关于家庭旅馆安排说了什么？
options: They have been the classic way to visit Europe.
They attract tourists with location and decoration.
They have long been competing with chain hotels.

questions.analysis: "B&Bs have been the classic way to visit Europe"，A 对应。D 与"not really a new idea"相反。

questions.prompt: What is the first thing you have to consider if you want to start a B&B business?
questions.promptZh: 如果你想开办家庭旅馆生意，你首先必须考虑什么？
options: Your financial status.
Your family's consent.
Your property.
Your personality.
questions.analysis: "The first consideration is your property"，C 对应。

questions.prompt: What does the speaker say potential B&B hosts must be realistic about?
questions.promptZh: 说话者说潜在的家庭旅馆经营者必须对什么有现实认识？
options: Costs for starting the business.
The number of guests to receive.
The facilities to provide.
Opportunities for income.
questions.analysis: "must be realistic about opportunities for income"，D 对应。

sections.title: News Report One（引擎盖下的猫）
sections.transcript:
A terrified cat has survived a five-mile round trip under the engine cover of a car on a school run. The black cat was found curled up under the engine cover of David King's car when he decided to do an oil check after dropping his grandson off at school in Kent.
Mr King's wife said her husband had come "running in" and was "shouting for me to come have a look".
"We weren't even sure it was alive, so I gently pushed it with a stick to check it was breathing and saw it was a terrified little cat. It reversed even further into the engine and was stuck. I tried to reach it, but it was too far down and there wasn't any way I could get it out."
Following a rescue by UK charity Cats Protection, the four-year-old cat was later reunited with its owner, Mr King's neighbour.
sections.transcriptZh:
一只受惊的猫在一辆汽车的引擎盖下完成了五英里的往返行程，这辆车当时正在接送孩子上学。当David King在Kent郡送完孙子上学后决定检查机油时，发现这只黑猫蜷缩在他汽车的引擎盖下。
King先生的妻子说，她丈夫"跑进来""喊我过去看看"。
"我们甚至不确定它是否还活着，所以我用一根棍子轻轻推了推它，确认它还在呼吸，发现是一只受惊的小猫。它往引擎深处又退了退，被卡住了。我试图够到它，但它在太深的地方，我没办法把它弄出来。"
经过英国慈善机构Cats Protection的救援，这只四岁的猫后来与它的主人——King先生的邻居团聚了。

questions.prompt: Where was the black cat found?
questions.promptZh: 这只黑猫是在哪里被发现的？
options: Outside the office of a charity foundation.
Inside the car of David King's neighbour.
Under the engine cover of a man's car.
At the gate of a grade school in Kent.
questions.analysis: 原文"found curled up under the engine cover of David King's car"，C对应。A慈善机构只是救援方，B邻居是猫的主人，D学校是送孙子上学的地方。

questions.prompt: What do we learn about the cat at the end of the news report?
questions.promptZh: 关于这只猫，新闻报道最后我们了解到什么？
options: It got reunited with its owner.
It was injured during the rescue.
It became a pet of Mr King's grandson.
It was placed in the care of a UK charity.
questions.analysis: 末句"the four-year-old cat was later reunited with its owner"，A对应。B受伤未提及，C孙子只是背景人物，D慈善机构是救援方不是最终归宿。

sections.title: News Report Two（特殊奥运会）
sections.transcript:
In less than a month, the Special Olympics Spring Games will make a return to Fayetteville. The Games are coming back for the first time in five years. The event will take place at Methodist University.
Event organizer Benjamin Kowalczyk says he's excited that athletes will get a chance to come back and demonstrate their abilities. Organizers expect about 100 athletes will come out to compete in Fayetteville. They will have a variety of events to choose from, including running, throwing, and jumping. There will also be a fun tent for children. Kowalczyk said it's rewarding to see athletes with special needs triumph in the Games.
For anyone who wants to help make this year's Games a massive success, there are still opportunities to volunteer for Fayetteville's Special Olympics. Organizers encourage them to visit the Games' website to sign up.
sections.transcriptZh:
不到一个月后，特殊奥林匹克春季运动会将重返Fayetteville。这是该运动会五年来首次回归。活动将在Methodist University举行。
活动组织者Benjamin Kowalczyk表示，他很高兴运动员们将有机会回来展示他们的能力。组织者预计约有100名运动员将来到Fayetteville参加比赛。他们将有多种项目可供选择，包括跑步、投掷和跳跃。现场还将设有儿童趣味帐篷。Kowalczyk说，看到有特殊需求的运动员在运动会上取得胜利是很有意义的。
对于任何想要帮助今年运动会取得巨大成功的人，仍有机会为Fayetteville特殊奥林匹克运动会做志愿者。组织者鼓励他们访问运动会网站进行报名。

questions.prompt: What will Fayetteville witness in less than a month?
questions.promptZh: 不到一个月后，Fayetteville将见证什么？
options: The 100th anniversary celebration of Methodist University.
The first important political event in the next five years.
The opening of the Special Olympics Spring Games.
The reunion of this year's Olympic gold medalists.
questions.analysis: 首句"the Special Olympics Spring Games will make a return"，C对应。A百年校庆未提及，B把五年首次回归偷换成政治事件，D把Special Olympics偷换成普通奥运会金牌得主。

questions.prompt: What did Benjamin Kowalczyk say is rewarding to see?
questions.promptZh: Kowalczyk说看到什么令人欣慰？
options: Volunteers visit the Games' website to sign up.
Athletes with special needs triumph in the Games.
Organizers devote their time and energy to the Games.
Children play in a fun tent and enjoy themselves fully.
questions.analysis: "it's rewarding to see athletes with special needs triumph in the Games"，B对应。A是志愿者报名指引，C评价对象不是组织者，D趣味帐篷只是顺带设施。

sections.title: News Report Three（巧克力兔子版权案）
sections.transcript:
A German supermarket has been ordered to destroy its chocolate rabbits after it lost a court battle with a Swiss chocolate manufacturer.
The Swiss firm had argued its gold-wrapped chocolate rabbit deserved copyright protection from a similar product sold by the budget supermarket.
Switzerland's highest court agreed and overturned a ruling last year by the country's commercial court that had sided with the supermarket. It ordered that all the imitation rabbits be destroyed, but suggested the chocolate needn't be wasted. It could be melted for use in other products.
It said even though there are some differences between the two products, there was still the possibility of confusion for consumers. The Swiss manufacturer's rabbit has a red bow and bell, while the German supermarket's has a green bow and bell. The colour of the wrapper is similar, as are the illustrations of the features.
The chocolate company has been to court before to protect its popular chocolate treat. Last year, a German federal court said the shade of the gold wrapping was also protected.
sections.transcriptZh:
一家德国超市在与一家瑞士巧克力制造商的法庭诉讼中败诉后，被勒令销毁其巧克力兔子产品。
这家瑞士公司辩称，其金色包装的巧克力兔子应当受到版权保护，以防止这家廉价超市销售的类似产品侵权。
瑞士最高法院表示同意，推翻了去年该国商事法院支持超市的裁决。法院下令销毁所有仿冒兔子产品，但建议巧克力无需浪费，可以融化用于其他产品。
法院称，尽管两种产品之间存在一些差异，但仍有可能使消费者产生混淆。瑞士制造商的兔子有红色蝴蝶结和铃铛，而德国超市的兔子有绿色蝴蝶结和铃铛。包装纸的颜色相似，特征的图案也相似。
这家巧克力公司此前曾诉诸法庭以保护其畅销巧克力产品。去年，德国联邦法院裁定金色包装纸的色调也受到保护。

questions.prompt: What has the German supermarket been ordered to do?
questions.promptZh: 这家德国超市被要求做什么？
options: Destroy its imitation chocolate rabbits.
Change the wrapping of its commodities.
Compensate for the Swiss manufacturer's loss.
Defend itself in the country's commercial court.
questions.analysis: "has been ordered to destroy its chocolate rabbits"，A对应。B改包装未提，C赔偿未提，D出庭辩护是旧判决场景。

questions.prompt: What did Switzerland's highest court suggest about the chocolate in question?
questions.promptZh: 瑞士最高法院对有关巧克力提出了什么建议？
options: It could be rewrapped and sold by the budget supermarket.
It could be reshaped into animals other than rabbits.
It could be resold cheaper to avoid waste.
It could be reused in other products.
questions.analysis: "the chocolate needn't be wasted. It could be melted for use in other products"，D对应。A重包装出售未提，B改形状未提，C降价转售未提。

questions.prompt: Why did Switzerland's highest court overturn the commercial court's ruling?
questions.promptZh: 瑞士最高法院为什么推翻商事法院的裁决？
options: To be fair to the German supermarkets.
To protect chocolate retailers' interests.
To boost the growth of the chocolate industry.
To prevent consumers' possible confusion.
questions.analysis: "there was still the possibility of confusion for consumers"，D对应。A方向相反，B把消费者偷换成零售商，C促进行业发展未提。

sections.title: Conversation One（素食主义者）
sections.transcript:
M: Can you please hand me that book over there? It has instructions for making a winter bean salad. My sister's boyfriend is coming over for dinner. He's vegetarian, so I need to make a lot of vegetable dishes.
W: He only eats vegetables, no meat? That doesn't sound like a very balanced diet. How can he get enough protein? What does he do to strengthen his muscles and all that?
M: Apparently that's no problem. He eats a variety of different vegetables and nuts, especially those with high amounts of protein.
W: It sounds a bit difficult, but he's done his research I suppose. What's his reasoning for being vegetarian? Is it his religion, health condition, or lifestyle?
M: He's an animal activist. He's always been very sensitive and sympathizes with animals. He's even written to his state senator about the torture of dolphins in sea parks. He says that keeping animals in zoos and parks causes them great distress.
W: That's a little gloomy, but I can understand that to a point. Not all zoos and animal parks have the most favorable conditions, but without them it just wouldn't be feasible to learn about animals and their environments. Besides, I don't think I could ever give up a good hot dog at a baseball game.
M: Honestly, I agree, but just don't let him hear you say that. He's the spokesperson for his local animal rights group.
sections.transcriptZh:
男：你能把那边那本书递给我吗？上面有冬季豆子沙拉的做法。我姐姐的男朋友要过来吃晚饭。他是素食主义者，所以我得做很多蔬菜菜肴。
女：他只吃蔬菜，不吃肉？这听起来可不像是均衡的饮食啊。他怎么获取足够的蛋白质？他怎么增强肌肉什么的？
男：显然这不是问题。他吃各种不同的蔬菜和坚果，尤其是那些蛋白质含量高的。
女：听起来有点难，不过我想他是做过研究的。他吃素的理由是什么？是宗教信仰、健康状况，还是生活方式？
男：他是个动物保护主义者。他一直很敏感，同情动物。他甚至给他所在州的参议员写信，抗议海洋公园虐待海豚。他说把动物关在动物园和公园里会给它们造成巨大的痛苦。
女：这有点悲观，不过我在某种程度上能理解。不是所有动物园和动物公园的条件都最理想，但没有它们的话，了解动物及其生存环境根本就不可行。再说，我觉得我永远都放弃不了在棒球赛上吃根美味热狗。
男：老实说，我同意，不过别让他听到你这么说。他是当地动物权利组织的发言人。

questions.prompt: What does the man request the woman to do?
questions.promptZh: 男士要求女士做什么？
options: Return the handbook to him.
Make a vegetable dish.
Pass a book to him.
Meet his sister's boyfriend.
questions.analysis: "Can you please hand me that book over there?"，C递书对应。A handbook是hand+book谐音陷阱，B做菜是男士自己做，D见男友只是背景。

questions.prompt: What does the woman say about eating vegetables only?
questions.promptZh: 关于只吃蔬菜，女士是怎么说的？
options: It doesn't seem to be a balanced diet.
It would reduce one's protein intake.
It would do harm to one's muscles.
It doesn't sound practical for her.
questions.analysis: "That doesn't sound like a very balanced diet"，A对应。B只是反问怎么获取蛋白，C没说伤肌肉，D没说对她不实际。

questions.prompt: Why does the boyfriend of the man's sister choose to be a vegetarian?
questions.promptZh: 男士的姐姐的男朋友为什么选择成为素食主义者？
options: To improve his health.
To protect animal rights.
To follow a trendy lifestyle.
To stick to his religious belief.
questions.analysis: "He's an animal activist"，B保护动物权利对应。A健康、C时尚、D宗教都是女士列举的待选项，不是真正原因。

questions.prompt: On what point does the man agree with the woman at the end of the conversation?
questions.promptZh: 在对话结束时，男士在哪一点上同意女士的观点？
options: The torture and distress dolphins suffer in parks.
The necessity of having zoos and eating meat.
The gloomy environments animals are kept in.
The urgency of joining an animal rights group.
questions.analysis: 男士结尾"Honestly, I agree"指向女士说的两点：动物园有必要+舍不得放弃热狗（吃肉），B对应。A是男友立场，C形容男友说法悲观，D未提。

sections.title: Conversation Two（时差与怕坐飞机）
sections.transcript:
W: Did you see that television program on air travel last night?
M: Yes. The part about overcoming jetlag was interesting. I was surprised that the expert recommended not eating for the entire journey and avoiding sleeping on the plane.
W: I was too, as I read an article on the subject in the past that suggested the opposite. It claimed that it was important not to miss meals and that taking a nap on the plane was the best way to adjust to a new time zone.
M: Well, the expert on the show did cite research supporting her recommendations, so I guess I'll give it a try next time I fly a long distance. Jetlag is a big problem for me and has been for the last few years, even though I never suffered from it before.
W: Well, she did say that jetlag often becomes more of a problem after 40, so I guess I'm lucky that I can still adjust to different time zones well. My problem is I'm afraid to fly.
M: Oh, I didn't know that. Actually, my mother is terrified of airplanes to the point where she can't even fly, so our family vacations were always by car or train.
W: I'm not as bad as that. I just get anxious before I fly and feel nervous the whole time we're in the air, which is why I was hoping the television program would cover that topic more than it did.
M: Yeah. That segment was too brief, especially as so many people have that problem. She said 20% of people are afraid to fly.
W: Actually, it was a quarter of people, so the problem really is widespread and deserves attention.
sections.transcriptZh:
女：你昨晚看那个关于航空旅行的电视节目了吗？
男：看了。关于克服时差反应那部分挺有意思的。我很惊讶那个专家建议整个旅程都不吃东西，还要避免在飞机上睡觉。
女：我也是，因为我以前读过一篇关于这个话题的文章，建议的是相反的做法。文章说不能错过用餐很重要，而且在飞机上小睡是适应新时区的最好方法。
男：嗯，节目里那位专家确实引用了研究来支持她的建议，所以我想下次长途飞行时试试看。时差反应对我来说是个大问题，过去几年一直这样，尽管我以前从来没有受过时差困扰。
女：嗯，她确实说过时差反应在40岁之后往往会变成更大的问题，所以我想我很幸运，还能很好地适应不同的时区。我的问题是我害怕坐飞机。
男：哦，我不知道这个。其实我妈妈特别害怕飞机，严重到根本不能坐飞机，所以我们家的假期总是开车或坐火车。
女：我没那么严重。我只是在坐飞机前会焦虑，在空中的整个过程都感到紧张，这就是为什么我希望那个电视节目能更多地讨论这个话题。
男：是啊。那个部分太简短了，特别是有那么多人都有这个问题。她说20%的人害怕坐飞机。
女：实际上是四分之一的人，所以这个问题确实很普遍，值得关注。

questions.prompt: What part of the TV program does the man say was interesting?
questions.promptZh: 男士说电视节目的哪部分内容很有趣？
options: The part about getting over jetlag.
The part about air travel in the past.
The part about not eating on board the plane.
The part about avoiding sleeping on the plane.
questions.analysis: "The part about overcoming jetlag was interesting"，A对应。C和D是专家建议让男士吃惊的内容，不是有趣的部分。

questions.prompt: What does the man say he will do next time he flies a long distance?
questions.promptZh: 男士说他下次长途飞行时会做什么？
options: Take a nap to adjust to a new time zone.
Have meals as usual to stay away from hunger.
Concentrate on reading articles recommended by experts.
Try following the advice given by the expert on the show.
questions.analysis: "I'll give it a try next time I fly a long distance"指试试专家建议，D对应。A是女士读到的旧观点，B与专家建议相反，C没说去读文章。

questions.prompt: Why does the woman think she is lucky?
questions.promptZh: 女士为什么认为自己很幸运？
options: She does not have any problem flying.
She can spend a lot of time vacationing.
She does not have to worry about jetlag.
She has been well treated when traveling.
questions.analysis: "I can still adjust to different time zones well"说明她不必担心时差，C对应。A与"我怕坐飞机"相反，B度假未提，D受优待未提。

questions.prompt: Why does the woman think the problem of being afraid to fly deserves attention?
questions.promptZh: 女士为什么认为害怕乘飞机的问题值得关注？
options: It has caused heavy losses to many airlines.
It impacts female travelers more seriously.
It has long been ignored by many experts.
It affects twenty-five percent of people.
questions.analysis: "it was a quarter of people, so the problem really is widespread and deserves attention"，四分之一=25%，D对应。A航空公司亏损未提，B影响女性更严重未提，C被专家忽视与原文相反。

sections.title: Passage One（UX设计入门）
sections.transcript:
The most common question I'm asked always centers around how to get started in user experience design, to which my response is always that nothing can substitute real-world experience.
Building the skills required of a user experience designer takes time, patience, and commitment. Higher education is a great way to equip yourself with some core skills, but it will not prepare you for actual challenges you'll face with clients' work. In other words, being proficient with a design tool and a few methods doesn't make you a user experience designer. There simply isn't a one-size-fits-all process.
Being effective requires adaptability — something you don't really learn in school, much less in a 6-month training camp. It's gained through experience on the job and learning what's appropriate given the needs of the project.
I found my way to user experience through graphic design and slowly over many different roles and experiences. That led me to become a user experience designer. It took time and commitment to continue to pursue roles within teams that I knew could teach and challenge me. That's not to say that I think my path is the only one. But once again, nothing can substitute real-world experience. You can start anywhere as long as you know your end goal and you commit to actively pursuing opportunities to learn and grow along the way.
sections.transcriptZh:
我被问到的最常见问题总是围绕如何开始从事用户体验设计，对此我的回答始终是，没有什么能替代真实世界的经验。
培养用户体验设计师所需的技能需要时间、耐心和投入。高等教育是让你具备一些核心技能的好方法，但它不会让你为客户工作中将面临的实际挑战做好准备。换句话说，精通一个设计工具和几种方法并不能让你成为用户体验设计师。根本不存在一个放之四海而皆准的流程。
要做到有效需要适应能力——这是你在学校里真正学不到的，更不用说在6个月的培训营中了。它是通过工作中的经验获得的。
我通过平面设计找到了进入用户体验的道路。这让我成为了一名用户体验设计师。这并不是说我认为我的道路是唯一的。但再次强调，没有什么能替代真实世界的经验。只要你知道自己的最终目标，并致力于积极寻求学习和成长的机会，你可以从任何地方开始。

questions.prompt: What does the speaker think is the best way to get started in user experience design?
questions.promptZh: 演讲者认为入门用户体验设计的最佳方式是什么？
options: Learning from skilled designers.
Obtaining real-world experience.
Joining a 6-month training camp.
Anticipating actual challenges.
questions.analysis: "nothing can substitute real-world experience"，B对应。A未提，C是反面例子，D预判挑战未提。

questions.prompt: What does the speaker say being effective requires?
questions.promptZh: 演讲者说要有效需要什么？
options: Core skills.
Higher education.
Adaptability.
Capability.
questions.analysis: "Being effective requires adaptability"，C原词对应。A和B都是被往下压的项，D是形近干扰。

questions.prompt: What can people do as long as they know their end goal and strive for it?
questions.promptZh: 只要人们知道自己的最终目标并为之努力，他们能做什么？
options: Start anywhere.
Face challenges.
Pursue roles in teams.
Follow their own path.
questions.analysis: "You can start anywhere as long as you know your end goal"，A对应。B和C是作者自己的经历，D与"我的路不是唯一的"相反。

sections.title: Passage Two（灵活座位）
sections.transcript:
When planning for this year, our principal asked what needed to change to engage students more in their learning. I responded in a whisper "flexible seating", thinking about our then-current classroom. It had rows of desks with blue chairs and nameplates reminding each student where they should be sitting.
This began a journey to transform our practice and challenge the ways of learning for a group of Year 6 students used to sitting in desks and rows for years.
Flexible seating has been defined as movable furniture to create an engaging learning environment. It is a shift in practice from being teacher-focused to student-focused learning. For us, flexible seating has meant removing most of the traditional chairs and desks and introducing a variety of different seating options to promote student engagement.
The use of rows and their minimal adaptations to "U" shape were traditionally intended to maximize on-task behavior and reduce distraction from the teacher. Teachers tend to still use this format because of either the need to control students or the belief that the teacher is the most important person in the room.
Now our students have a range of different seating options, including a floor desk, couches, stools, bean bags, and the traditional desk-and-chair.
From our experience so far, flexible seating enhances student ownership of space and engagement in learning, while reducing rates of student disengagement and disciplinary actions. It is a win for all concerned.
sections.transcriptZh:
在规划今年的工作时，我们的校长问需要改变什么才能让学生更多地参与到学习中来。我小声回答"灵活座位"。
灵活座位被定义为可移动的家具，用以创造一个富有吸引力的学习环境。它是从以教师为中心向以学生为中心学习的实践转变。对我们而言，灵活座位意味着移除大部分传统的椅子和课桌，引入各种不同的座位选择来促进学生参与。
现在我们的学生有一系列不同的座位选择，包括地板书桌、沙发、凳子、豆袋椅以及传统的课桌椅。
根据我们迄今为止的经验，灵活座位增强了学生对空间的所有权和学习参与度，同时降低了学生脱离学习和纪律处分的比率。这对所有相关方来说都是双赢。

questions.prompt: Why did the school principal ask what needed to change?
questions.promptZh: 校长为什么要问需要改变什么？
options: To respond actively to students' requests.
To engage students more in their learning.
To enable teachers to interact more with their students.
To allow students more freedom in their academic work.
questions.analysis: "what needed to change to engage students more in their learning"，B对应。A学生请求未提，C师生互动偷换主体，D学业自由过度推断。

questions.prompt: What has flexible seating meant at the speaker's school?
questions.promptZh: 灵活座位在说话者的学校意味着什么？
options: Using new furniture to create a comfortable environment.
Shifting from traditional teaching to task-based learning.
Adopting a variety of different seating options.
Rearranging most traditional chairs and desks.
questions.analysis: "flexible seating has meant...introducing a variety of different seating options"，C对应。A舒适环境未提，B任务式学习偷换概念，D是撤掉不是重排。

questions.prompt: What has flexible seating brought about at the speaker's school?
questions.promptZh: 灵活座位在说话者的学校带来了什么？
options: A win for all people involved.
A strengthened effect of its discipline.
A harmonious relationship among its students.
A change to teachers' opinion of their students.
questions.analysis: "It is a win for all concerned"，A对应。B方向相反（减少纪律处分），C同学关系未提，D老师看法未提。

sections.title: Passage Three（英国校服鞋事件）
sections.transcript:
Dozens of British students arriving for their first day of school on Tuesday were sent home over their shoes. About 30 students were turned away from Taverham High School in Norfolk, England. Headteacher, Dr Roger Harris, confirmed that this was due to a change in the school's uniform policy. Harris, who became headteacher this year, said he notified parents of the updated rules in an email in June.
The price of school uniforms can spark panic among families struggling with the high cost of living. Nearly all British schools have uniforms. They cost parents an average of £337 per year for each secondary school child.
According to the new rules, students of Taverham are required to wear smart black shoes appropriate for the workplace, Harris held that strengthened rules around school uniforms improved student outcomes and behavior. But for some parents, the school's restrictions are an unnecessary burden.
As annual inflation climbs over 10%, many households are on tight budgets. Private rental prices in Britain rose 3.2% over the 12 months to July 2022, the largest jump since 2016. Soaring energy bills have made things worse.
Lucinda May, mum of a Taverham student, said that she had to ask her parents for £65 to buy her child the correct pair of shoes. May said that the school's uniform policy showed the lack of regard for parents dealing with the high cost of living.
sections.transcriptZh:
周二，数十名英国学生因鞋子问题在开学第一天被遣返回家。英格兰诺福克郡Taverham高中约有30名学生被拒之门外。校长Roger Harris博士证实，这是由于学校校服政策的变化。
校服价格可能让那些苦于高昂生活成本的家庭感到恐慌。几乎所有英国学校都有校服。家长平均每年为每个中学生支付337英镑的校服费用。
根据新规定，Taverham的学生必须穿适合职场的得体黑色鞋子。Harris认为，加强校服规定能改善学生的学业成绩和行为表现。但对一些家长来说，学校的限制是不必要的负担。
随着年通胀率攀升至10%以上，许多家庭的预算都很紧张。
Taverham学生家长Lucinda May说，她不得不向父母要65英镑给孩子买一双符合规定的鞋子。

questions.prompt: Why were dozens of British students sent home on Tuesday?
questions.promptZh: 为什么数十名英国学生在周二被送回家？
options: They weren't informed of the school's updated rules.
They arrived late for their first day of school.
They answered their headteacher's email in an impolite way.
They didn't wear the shoes required by the school's new policy.
questions.analysis: "sent home over their shoes" + "due to a change in the school's uniform policy"，D对应。A与"6月已邮件通知"相反，B迟到未提，C不礼貌回邮件未提。

questions.prompt: What can the price of school uniforms spark among families in financial difficulty?
questions.promptZh: 校服的价格会在经济困难的家庭中引发什么？
options: Riots.
Anger.
Disputes.
Panic.
questions.analysis: "can spark panic among families struggling with the high cost of living"，D对应。A骚乱过度夸大，B愤怒未提，C争执未提。

questions.prompt: What did the headteacher think of the school's new uniform rules?
questions.promptZh: 校长如何看待学校的新校服规定？
options: They strengthened the school's discipline and order.
They improved student behavior and performance.
They enhanced the positive image of the school.
They rendered the school unique in the district.
questions.analysis: "strengthened rules around school uniforms improved student outcomes and behavior"，B对应。A把strengthened对象偷换成纪律，C正面形象未提，D地区独树一帜未提。

questions.prompt: What did Lucinda May have to do to buy her child the correct pair of shoes?
questions.promptZh: Lucinda May为了给孩子买到正确的鞋子必须做什么？
options: Turn to her parents for help.
Tighten her monthly budget.
Borrow £65 from her friend.
Postpone paying her other bills.
questions.analysis: "she had to ask her parents for £65"，A向父母求助对应。B缩预算是大环境不是她的动作，C把parents偷换成friend，D推迟账单未提。
